item.title: A Gym for Theory
item.description: Hardly anyone who worked the fields ever felt the need for a gym. We go to the gym because our jobs stopped asking anything of our bodies: machines took over the effort, and we had to invent a place where we could put it back on purpose. The Greeks, who gave us the word, already knew the pattern. Their gymnasia were meant for free citizens, while slaves, who did most of the work with their hands, were barred by law.

item.title: Why Not Straight to Assembly?
item.description: I was thinking, just a question. Whenever I ask an LLM for something computational, I get Python back. I tried with the ones I use, and the answer is always the same. Wouldn’t it be better to get something lower level, say assembly directly? I am no expert on the subject at all, and the question was already lurking at the end of another post.

item.title: These Are All English Words
item.description: A few weeks ago I showed a professor the latest developments of the framework we are building together. Among them was something I was rather proud of: an MCP server, a layer that lets a language model use the framework directly, building models, running analyses, reading results. He scrolled through the code for a while, frowned, and said: “But these are all English words.”

item.title: Who Else Read My Proposal?
item.description: It is no secret that this year I resubmitted my MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposal. Unfortunately, it does not reflect what is happening in the world right now, something I touched on briefly in my previous post and plan to come back to here soon. Still, the resubmission left me with a thought I cannot shake off.

item.title: The Elephant in the Session Room
item.description: Five days in Berlin for ECEE 2026, and what lingers is not a talk but a feeling of unease. Not because of the science: the science was excellent. Professor Cotton’s keynote on ground-motion models in the age of big data was among the most stimulating talks I have heard in a while, and Professor Vamvatsikos confirmed once again his gift for metaphors that are daring and yet pedagogically flawless.
